findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation 

Inspector observed mashed potatoes, brown gravy, and white gravy to be stored beyond the 7-day date mark in the “Monster Energy” cooler. The PIC was informed and the items were discarded. Ensure staff are checking coolers at the start or end of each day and discarding any items beyond the 7-day mark. 

Inspector observed deli beef and deli turkey in the bottom of the cook line prep cooler to be stored past its 7-day date mark. The beef was marked 2/24 and the turkey was marked 2/23. Ensure staff are monitoring coolers daily and discarding any items stored beyond 7 days. The items were discarded during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a mouse on a glue trap in the back storage area of the facility. The PIC was informed and plans to contact pest control for treatment. Inspector recommends ensuring all outer openings are properly sealed and the exterior of the building is treated for pests. Ensure all food items in the dry storage area are protected from rodents. Inspector recommends placing any food items in plastic or cardboard into hard plastic bins. A follow-up will be conducted on August 31, 2026 to ensure all pests have been removed from the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the floors around the fryers to have an accumulation of grease and dust debris. Ensure these areas are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw corned beef stored on top of bagged soft serve mix in the back room upright cooler. The PIC was informed and stated that she is training new opening staff that failed to order the cooler correctly. The beef was moved to the bottom of the cooler during the inspection. Ensure staff are educated on proper storage order policy to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The prep cooler next to the grill in the kitchen was observed to be inoperable during today’s inspection. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods stored in the cooler are being monitored with time as a control until the cooler is repaired. Ensure TCS foods in the cooler are kept for no longer than 4 hours. Items kept in the cooler for 4 hours must be discarded; they cannot be cooled and reused. A follow-up is scheduled for July 25th to ensure the cooler has been repaired.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple food service employees fail to wash hands before donning a new pair of gloves. PIC was informed and education was conducted regarding proper hand washing practices. Ensure staff are washing hands before donning new gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: The upright freezer in the kitchen was observed to have an accumulation of ice. The ice accumulation is at risk of contacting food in the freezer, resulting in cross-contamination. The PIC is aware of the issue and is storing food such that it does not contact the ice in the freezer. Ensure the freezer is repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-303.12 Storage or Display of Food in Contact with Water or Ice. (A) PACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if the FOOD is subject to the entry of water because of the nature of its packaging, wrapping, or container or its positioning in the ice or water (B) Except as specified in (C) and (D) of this section, unPACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with undrained ice. (C) Whole, raw fruits or vegetables; cut, raw vegetables such as celery or carrot sticks or cut potatoes; and tofu may be immersed in ice or water. (D) Raw poultry and raw FISH that are received immersed in ice in shipping containers may remain in that condition while in storage awaiting preparation, display, service, or sale.

findings.comment: Observed ice cream novelties and quarts and pints of ice cream to be packaged in advance of retail sale with no labels. 750-110g Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name;, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used. Properly label items.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed house made strawberry topping in the facility that is date marked 4-17.  House made items must be 7 day date marked and used or discarded. 750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days. Discussed making topping and freezing half so that the time can be stopped and the product kept for more than 7 days. Use freeze date tags on these like other items in the facility.  The topping was discarded.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: Observed the hood vent to be soiled. 750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: Observed employee food to be stored with other food for sale to the public. 750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings. Food items were separated.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - A) Heavy ice buildup was observed on/around the condenser in the 4 door cooler located in back storage. One of the fans appeared to be hindered from the buildup. Defrost the unit as needed to minimize ice accumulation, which allow for proper function of the unit as well as ease in cleaning/maintenance.

B) Shelf above hot holding unit at the far end of the cook line was soiled with what appeared to be salt/pepper accumulation. The trim along the front edge of the shelf was also loose, and what appeared to be salt/pepper accumulation was observed in the area of disrepair. Clean and repair the shelf.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Faucet at 3 part sink was observed with leaks at nuts and junctures. Repair the faucet so it does not leak.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - A) (R) Damaged floor tiles were observed under the cooking equipment. One tile under the left fryer had a chunk missing. A gap was present between tiles under the right fryer, and tiles under the left end of the flat grill also had chunks missing. As of the 8/23/16 routine inspection the owner stated they replaced the tiles in front of the fryers and were in the process of completing floor tile repairs on the cook line under equipment. Tiles were to be replaced by the next routine inspection. Finish replacing tiles under equipment on the cook line.
The floor under the fryers was also observed to be soiled with grease and food debris. Clean the floor under fryers daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

B) Floor to wall juncture had a gap at the wall across from the cook line where baseboard was removed for repairs. Owners began removing plastic baseboard and steam cleaning prior to 8/23/16 routine inspection. Painted wood trim is supposed to be used to re-seal the areas where plastic baseboard was removed (see general comments of 8/23/16 inspection). Provide proper repairs and seal the floor to wall juncture at the wall across from the cook line.

Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
(R) 750.1210 - A) A few ceiling tiles in the front prep area were acoustic (above prep cooler at cook line). Coke was working on the lines back in March. As of the 8/23/16 routine inspection, owners stated smooth, cleanable tiles were purchased but were not yet installed. Tiles were to be replaced by the next routine inspection. Replace the ceiling tiles over the prep cooler with smooth, easily cleanable, non-absorbant tiles. 
 
B) Area of disrepair (potential water damage) was observed at the bottom of the wall on the right side of the ice cream topping/single service dry storage cooler (dessert area). Debris has begun to accumulate in the area where the wall is damaged. Repair the wall beneath the topping/dry storage cooler.

Walls and ceilings must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.citation_text:
750.1390 - Damp mops were observed in the mop closet stored with heads down in mop buckets. Store wet mop heads hanging or inverted between uses to allow for proper drying.

Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored properly.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.250 - Portion of roast beef in the top holding area of the prep cooler had surface and internal temperatures of 52F/54F and 49F respectively. The portion in question was stacked above the fill line, and the owners noted the lid was open for a period of time while cleaning up a spill within the cooler (may have caused elevated temperature). Portion of roast beef in question was discarded. Surface temperature of a portion further down in the pan was at 39F.
 
Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) shall be kept at 41F/below while on display and service.
NOTE: Be careful when filling containers of food. Make sure portions of PHF and items such as sour cream packets are not stacked so high that they can not be maintained at proper temperature when stored in the top of the prep cooler.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee was observed handling money at the cash register and then ice cream orders were immediately prepared without washing hands. Handwashing between tasks was discussed with owners/employee. Hands were properly washed before continuing with food prep.

Hands must be properly washed any time they may have been contaminated and prior to handling food, clean equipment, and single service articles.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - Floor tiles under fryers were damaged. Owners recently replaced tiled in front of the fryers, and are in the process of completing floor tile repairs on the cook line under equipment. Tiles will be replaced by next routine inspection.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1210 - A) A few ceiling tiles in the front prep area were acoustic. Coke was working on the lines back in March. Smooth, cleanable tiles were purchased but have yet to be installed. Replace the ceiling tiles by the next routine inspection. 
 
B) Area of disrepair (potential water damage) was observed at the bottom of the wall on the right side of the ice cream topping/single service dry storage cooler. Debris has begun to accumulate in the area where the wall is damaged. Repair the wall beneath the topping/dry storage cooler.

Walls and ceilings must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Grilled onions in the top holding area of prep cooler had surface and internal temperatures of 46F-56F and 50F-60F respectively. Cook stated he began prepping/cooking onions around 8a and started cooling process around 830a. Onions were already below 70F and had another 4hrs to get to 41F/below. Cook provided label to indicate when cooling began and was advised to check the temperatures/verify onions reach 41F/below by 230p if they are not all used by that time.

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F.
Track the time and temperature during the cooling process, and use ice baths to rapidly drop temperatures of cooling foods prior to placing products in coolers. Putting hot food directly in the cooler could compromise the unit and other products inside.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Trays with frozen ham and roast beef portions were observed on top of the prep cooler. Cooked stated they were frozen solid and just pulled from the freezer. Frozen products should not be allowed to sit at room temperature for any amount of time. Roast beef and ham portions were placed in the bottom holding area of the prep cooler.

Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the following methods: 1. Under refrigeration 41F/below, 2. Under  potable running water 70F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Milkshake mixing wands and surfaces above wands were soiled with food splash from the previous evening.

Manually wash, rinse, and sanitize milk shake mixing wands and all surfaces above/around the wands up to every 4hrs after continuous use. Between 4hr intervals wipe down food contact surfaces between orders as needed.
Make sure the milkshake machine is getting cleaned and sanitized at the close of business daily. If the machine is left soiled and nobody checks it prior to use the following day there is potential for cross contamination and to make someone sick.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - A) Floor tiles under fryers were damaged, and grease/debris accumulation was starting to occur. Clean under the fryers, and replace damaged floor tiles.

B) Floors were soiled with food/general debris under the 4 door coolers and 2 door freezer by the back office area. Clean the floors under coolers and freezers as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Four pans of cheese sauce were observed cooling on the prep table in back. Surface and internal temperatures were 93F-97F and 107F respectively. Employee doing prep had a note in front of the containers that said cool to 40F before placing in refrigerator. Employee stated the cooling process began within the last hour, and pans were on an ice bath initially. Employee stated the final cooking temperature was 174F, but a temperature was not taken to know where product was at prior to being pulled from ice baths. Pans of cheese sauce were placed back on ice baths. Owner and staff were advised to closely monitor the temperature of the cheese sauce, stir it frequently, and keep adding ice to surround the containers in the ice bath while the cooling process is in progress. 

Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in an additional 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. The only way to know foods are cooling properly is to check temperatures with clean calibrated stem thermometers. Monitor the time and temperature of cooing foods to ensure products are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frame.
Label cooling foods with date and time of prep.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee went from washing dishes to taking a customer's order and did not wash hands before preparing to make a drink. Employee was advised on handwashing between tasks. Hands were washed prior to continuing with drink prep.

Hands must be properly washed between tasks, any time hands may become contaminated, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - A) Microwave safe containers used for heating BBQ pork were pitted and rough in several spots on the food contact surfaces. Containers were discarded in the trash.

B) Large white plastic ice scoop was cracked along the handle. Replace the ice scoop.
 
Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sanitizer bucket at grill had a concentration of less than 200ppm quat (~100ppm). Solution was emptied; new solution was prepared at proper concentration from the wall mounted dispenser (200ppm).
Other sanitizer solutions were observed at 200-400ppm at the counter and soft serve areas. 

Change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more often if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled. Frequent use will wear the solution down at an accelerated rate. Maintain quat sanitizer solutions at 200-400ppm.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text:
750.1160 - Several small, black ants were observed around the walk-up window next to the cash register. Inner glass window was closed, but outside screen was torn at the bottom right side (pulled away from the frame). Manager on duty eliminated ants from the area/cleaned general surfaces. Owner was advised the screen must be fixed in order to have the inner window open at the walk-up area for any length of time.
(see general comments)

Effective measures to minimize the presence of pests shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floor in the grill area was soiled with food debris and/or grease behind the reach-in freezer, along the wall behind/under the dry storage cooler, and under the fryers.
Clean the floor in the grill area under/behind all equipment as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Hamburger balls in bottom drawer of grill cooler had internal temperature of 52F-53F. Label on lid showed prep date of 3/15. Cook stated the pan was in the cooler overnight. Hamburger balls were discarded in the trash. All other foods had internal temperatures of 42F-44F (cook getting in/out for morning prep).

Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) shall be maintained at a proper temperature of 41F/below at all times during storage.
NOTE: There did not appear to be an issue with the cooler.  Closely monitor the cold holding temperatures of the grill cooler and PHF held inside. Make sure proper labels are on foods to avoid confusion.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text:
750.210 - Cheese sauce in steam well had surface and internal temperatures of 100F and 38F-64F respectively. Cook stated the cheese sauce was heated in the microwave prior to being placed in the steam well, and according to his thermometer the cheese sauce reached 155F. Cook was advised reheating temperature is 165F, the thermometer should be calibrated to make sure it is accurate, and the temperature needs to be checked in the middle of the product (thermal center). Cheese sauce was pulled from steam well and placed on grill to rapidly reheat to 165F/higher.

PHF shall be reheated rapidly to 165F/higher throughout the product within 2hrs. Properly reheat all foods to 165F/above. Use clean, calibrated thermometer to check temperatures and verify foods are properly reheated. Stir foods frequently during reheating process to help evenly distribute heat throughout foods.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sanitizer buckets on grill line were at 0ppm and less than 200ppm quat. Bucket at 0ppm only had a small amount of liquid in it. Cook was advised all wiping cloths must be submerged in solutions between uses. More RTU spray was added to bucket that tested at 0ppm (resulting concentration 200ppm). The other made from wall mounted solution was remade at proper concentration (200ppm). 

Maintain sanitizer solutions at 200-400ppm (directions on label). Change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more often if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled. Frequent use will wear the solution down at an accelerated rate. Always follow instructions on labels. Use warm water to dissolve Steramine tablets (see label for details).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Canisters of whipped topping (6 total; 1 opened/in-use) in small Coke cooler at sundae prep area had internal temperature of 50F-51F. Canisters were in the cooler overnight. Owner discarded whipped topping canisters in the trash. Air was blowing out of the cooler at 47F-48F. Boxes of apple juice and bottled water were the only other products in the cooler. New canisters of whipped topping (33F) were placed in the topping cooler, which was holding below 41F.
Maintain cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) at 41F/below at all times during storage. Do not use the small Coke cooler for storage of whipped topping or any other PHF unless the thermostat can be adjusted to drop the temperature in the cooler and maintain foods at 41F/below.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text: 750.510 - Employee was observed washing hands without use of the proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Owner spoke with employee about handwashing technique to reiterate the importance of proper handwashing. In order to avoid re-contamination of freshly washed hands, employees must always use paper towels as a barrier when shutting off the manual faucet at the handsink.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Milkshake mixing wands  were soiled with splash from the previous operating day. Mixing wands were cleaned and sanitized during the inspection.
Make sure mixing wands are being properly cleaned and sanitized at 4hr intervals throughout the day and at close of business.
Food contact surfaces must be properly cleaned and sanitized between uses/as needed (up to every 4hrs) to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - A) Floor tile was loose under the front leg of the 4 door cooler in the back storage area. Re-seal the tile to floor.
B) Floors were soiled along walls with food debris and/or single service articles in the following areas:
1. under dry storage cooler on cook line;
2. under dry storage cooler at sundae prep area;
3. under 4 door cooler in back storage; and
4. under onion storage bins.
Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas and throughout the facility as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.
Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Sour cream cups in top layers of pan in prep cooler had internal temperature of 52F-54F. Sour cream cups in the bottom of the pan had an internal temperature of 38F. Cook noted portions were in the prep cooler for ~30 minutes. Portions were separated into two pans, and some sour cream cups were placed back in the storage cooler. All portions of sour cream quickly dropped to 41F/below. Owners and staff were advised to not overfill pans past the fill lines to help maintain colder temperatures for potentially hazardous foods (PHF) in the top holding compartment of prep cooler.
Cold PHF shall be maintained at 41F/below. Maintain cold PHF at proper holding temperature.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Cold water handle of handsink was loose, and water was not dispensing properly. Cold water handle was repaired during the inspection to allow for proper flow of both hot and cold running water during handwashing.
All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair/maintain fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.151 - Four containers of cheese sauce in cooler were not labeled. Staff noted cheese sauce was made on 6/23. Benefit of doubt was given. Product was kept for use and properly dated. Ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods (PHF) must be properly dated and consumed, sold, or discarded within 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Reach-in cooler with milk and bulk ice cream mix at ice cream station did not have a thermometer inside. Provide a thermometer for the reach-in cooler. Make sure all coolers and freezers used for the storage of PHF have functioning thermometers in them in order to adequately monitor the temperature of units and products stored inside. All refrigeration units and freezers used to hold PHF shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - A) Grill freezer had heavy frost buildup inside. De-frost the grill freezer. B) Wood blocks under legs of flat grill are starting to crack and pull apart. Replace the wood blocks with once that are in good repair and can be easily cleaned. C) Waste tray of ice cream machine is cracked into two pieces and has a crack in the front on the right side. Repair the tray or replace it (do not use tape for repairs). Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) inside microwave (food splash); B) drip guard of ice machine (mold at crevice near ceiling and along front); & C) fan on top of corner ice cream machine (dust). Clean and sanitize all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. **In-use utensils such as tongs and knives must be switched out with clean utensils up to every 4 hours and properly cleaned and sanitized.**

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) (R) general surfaces of cook line equipment - sides and underneath surfaces of fryers & grill, top of cooler under grill, inside fryer panels around mechanicals, legs of equipment, & attached plumbing/lines; B) cabinets used for single service storage (old mouse droppings in the two closest to cook line); C) back of grill freezer (heavy dust buildup); & D) floor fan blowing on motor of ice cream machine (dust). Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.860 - Cleaned/sanitized ketchup squeeze bottles/lids and cups for mixing milk shakes were observed air drying in the back prep area. Condensation from a cold water line was dripping down onto the bottles, cups, and lids. Staff noted the items would be washed/sanitized again. Cleaned and sanitized utensils/equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. **Do note store any clean equipment, single service articles, or food items directly below water lines**

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text: 750.880 - A) Little storage bins holding single service portion cups and lids were observed to be soiled with crumbs/splash. Clean the storage bins and maintain them clean to protect items from potential contamination. B) Cabinets with single service items had old mouse droppings inside (see #23 Part B). Staff were advised to discard any items not inside intact packaging and to wipe down outer surfaces of intact packaging with sanitizer solution. Thoroughly clean out cabinets before placing products back inside. Single-service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner which prevents protects them from contamination.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Soap was not available in men's restroom. Maintain supplies of soap and paper towels at all handsinks to allow for proper handwashing.
A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory. *Staff placed soap in the restroom during the inspection*

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Floors were soiled in the following areas: 1) (R) under cook line equipment; 2) (R) under meat cooler in back storage area; 3) under dry storage shelves in office/storage area; & 4) along walls/in corners of storage/prep/dish areas. Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas/throughout as needed to eliminate buildup of debris. B) Baseboard was loose at the corner behind the men's room toilet, and moisture has accumulated behind it. Clean/dry behind the baseboard and re-seal it to the wall.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 - A) (R) Trim was loose around the ceiling vent above the grill line prep cooler. Re-attach the trim to the wall. B) Holes were observed in the ceiling of the men's room around the light/vent. Repair the ceiling. C) Holes were observed in the wall behind toilet paper dispenser in employee restroom. Repair the wall in the employee restroom. **Go through facility and make any necessary repairs to walls, floor to wall junctures and ceilings.**

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text: 750.1300 & 1310 - Spray bottle was observed sitting on a shelf at the far left end of cook line next to single service articles and a bag of chips. Spray bottle was not labeled as to the contents. Chemical did not test with quat or chlorine test strips. Staff noted the bottle contained degreaser. Bottle was labeled and placed in proper chemical storage area. Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law and stored separate from food and all food related items (i.e. clean equipment & single service articles). Properly label and store containers of toxic substances.
